paper.title: Credit Where Credit Is Due: Contrastive Attribution Topology Search for Multi-Agent Systems
paper.abstract: An LLM multi-agent system (MAS) is only as good as the agents it chooses to trust: its accuracy and cost hinge on its topology, meaning which agents are included and how they communicate. A single task score, however, does not reveal which agents help or hinder performance. We propose Contrastive Attribution Topology Search (CATS), which searches for compact teams within a fixed supergraph of specialized agents. An LLM attributer compares execution traces across candidate topologies and assigns credit to individual agents. CATS uses these credits to update supergraph edges while progressively pruning weak edges and agents, yielding a small team for deployment. With small open-weight models and matched candidate evaluations, CATS improves mean accuracy on BigCodeBench by 5.3 percentage points over score-only heuristic search while using 54$\%$ fewer deployment tokens. On MBPP, CATS matches the strongest baselines with fewer tokens than the other searches. In a HotpotQA prompt-poisoning stress test, CATS excludes all adversarially prompted agents in all three runs, whereas random search retains some at comparable accuracy. Per-agent credit thus supports both team optimization and the pruning of potentially harmful agents.

one_sentence.text: 针对团队分数难以识别个体贡献的问题，CATS从固定智能体池出发，以跨候选轨迹归因更新通信边概率并剪枝；作者报告，在候选评估次数匹配时，BigCodeBench准确率比仅分数搜索高5.3个百分点，部署token少54%。

evidence.quote: Scores alone thus say little about which agents to keep.
We introduce Contrastive Attribution Topology Search (CATS) , an offline meta-agent that assembles teams from a fixed agent pool.
An LLM compares their transcripts and assigns each agent signed credit. CATS then updates link probabilities, prunes weak links and unreachable agents, and selects one fixed team for deployment.

Our selected topology G^{\star} improves mean accuracy over the strongest baseline, score-only heuristic search, by 5.3 points while using 54% fewer deployment tokens with matched candidate evaluations (Table 1 ).

research_problem.text: 团队总分不足以指导个体保留：正确解答可能包含冗余工作，失败解答也可能包含有用贡献。

evidence.quote: Task scores, however, evaluate the team as a whole: a correct solution may contain unnecessary work, and a failed one may include useful contributions. Scores alone thus say little about which agents to keep.

method_steps.text: 以人工构造的领域专用完全DAG为候选母图（supergraph），用边logit定义采样概率；每步独立采样K个候选拓扑，拒绝包含源节点不可达节点的图。

evidence.quote: We search for an optimized multi-agent topology as a subgraph of a hand-crafted complete directed acyclic graph specialized to a chosen problem domain (Figure 1 ).
Each edge e carries a logit \theta_{e} with sampling probability \alpha_{e}=\sigma(\theta_{e}) , initialized to a common \alpha_{0} .
At each step, we sample K topologies by independently drawing e\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\alpha_{e}) , rejecting graphs with nodes unreachable from the source.

method_steps.text: 执行候选后，LLM归因器比较同题轨迹，根据任务分数、受长度限制的输出、工具调用及最终产物，分配[-1,1]个体信用；减去任务内平均信用，再跨有信用记录的任务取平均，得到节点优势。

evidence.quote: An LLM attributer assigns each participating agent i in candidate k on task q a credit c_{k,q,i}\in[-1,1] (harmful to helpful) by comparing candidate rollouts on the same task.
The attributer sees task scores, length-capped agent outputs, tool calls, and the final artifact state (e.g., the coding environment), and runs in parallel across tasks.

Credits are normalized into per-agent advantages A_{k,i}=|Q_{k,i}|^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q_{k,i}}(c_{k,q,i}-b_{q}) , where Q_{k,i} holds the tasks with a credit for i in k and b_{q} is the mean credit over participating agents and candidates for task q .

method_steps.text: 按目标节点优势更新已触发边的logit；指向活跃节点的未触发非源边接受较小更新。逐步剪除低概率边及不可达节点；最终仅从第T步候选选平均分最高者，平分优先成员少、再优先出现早者。

evidence.quote: Each edge (u,v) fired in candidate k is updated by \theta_{uv}\leftarrow\theta_{uv}+\eta A_{k,v} . Unfired non-source edges into an active agent v receive a smaller secondary update \theta_{uv}\leftarrow\theta_{uv}+\eta\rho A_{k,v} .

After each step we prune weak edges whose probability has fallen below the fraction \delta of its initial value (the pruning fraction ), E\leftarrow\{e\in E:\alpha_{e}\geq\delta\alpha_{0}\} , and remove nodes that are no longer reachable from the source.

After T steps we return the best final candidate G^{\star}=\arg\max_{k}\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{q}s_{k,q} over the step- T candidates, which are sampled under the accumulated priors. Ties are broken in favor of fewer agents and then the earlier candidate.

author_contributions.text: 作者自述贡献包括：用对比式个体信用指导团队构建、改善两项编码基准的准确率和部署token，以及在HotpotQA压力测试中排除投毒成员；不据此确认创新优先权。

evidence.quote: Our contributions are: (i) contrastive per-agent credit to guide team construction (Figure 1 ), (ii) higher mean accuracy and lower deployment token use than score-only search on two coding benchmarks with matched candidate evaluations (Table 1 )
(iii) a HotpotQA stress test where CATS excludes all poisoned agents in every run, while random search retains some at comparable accuracy (Table 2 ).

author_contributions.text: 作者将BigCodeBench归因适配描述为：评分持久化代码产物而非智能体文本，并提供有序、精简的工具效果。

evidence.quote: We adapt contrastive attribution [ 14 ] for BigCodeBench by grading the persisted code artifact instead of agent text. We also expose ordered, compact tool effects.

reported_comparisons.text: 本文比较无工具直接调用、ReAct单智能体、人工MAS、随机拓扑搜索及仅分数启发式搜索；两种搜索基线匹配同题K×T次候选评估，不匹配计算量。

evidence.quote: We compare against (i) a direct LLM call without tools, (ii) a ReAct [ 13 ] single agent, both with literature-derived system prompts (Appendix Table 6 ), (iii) a hand-crafted multi-agent system (MAS) designed before observing supergraph results (Appendix Figure 4(d) )

(iv) random topology search, and (v) a score-only heuristic search using CATS’s fired/unfired update and hyperparameters, with scalar task scores replacing agent credits. Both search baselines match K\times T candidate evaluations on the same tasks, not compute

reported_comparisons.text: 随机搜索以固定α=0.15抽取16个候选；仅分数搜索给活跃智能体相同的候选分数优势，沿用CATS更新与剪枝。作者明确该启发式缺少REINFORCE所需的伯努利得分函数因子。

evidence.quote: Random search Draw 16 candidates at fixed \alpha=0.15 .

Assign A_{k} to every active agent and update edge logits using the same learning rate, unfired-edge rule, and pruning schedule as our method, but without LLM attribution. This heuristic omits the Bernoulli score-function factor I_{e}-\alpha_{e} required by REINFORCE [ 11 ] .

reported_comparisons.text: 消融比较最终候选G*与剪枝后全部剩余节点和边组成的Gp；作者报告部署G*使编码token约减半，BigCodeBench平均准确率更高，MBPP相同。

evidence.quote: As an ablation, we also evaluate the pruned supergraph G_{\mathrm{p}} , consisting of all nodes and edges that remain after pruning.
Deploying G^{\star} instead of G_{\mathrm{p}} roughly halves coding deployment tokens, with higher mean accuracy on BigCodeBench and the same on MBPP (Table 1 ).

limitations.text: 作者将信用视为优化信号而非因果贡献；未用人类判断验证，且归因器能看见任务分数，信用与成功的相关性仅是内部一致性检查。

evidence.quote: so we treat our credit as an optimization signal, not a causal measure.
Attribution credits have not been validated against human judgments. Credit–success correlation (Table 9 ) is only a consistency check, since the attributer sees system_score .

limitations.text: 仅分数基线未单独调参，无法隔离组件贡献；节点信用等量传播至已触发入边，与Graph-GRPO边级信用的比较留待未来。评估仅覆盖一个模型家族、三个领域、三个种子，token成本只追踪而未优化。

evidence.quote: The score-only baseline was not separately tuned and does not isolate which component of CATS accounts for the difference.
Credit is node-level, propagated equally to all incoming fired edges. A comparison with Graph-GRPO’s statistical edge-level credit remains future work [ 3 ] .
Evaluating a single model family across three domains and three seeds limits what we can conclude about broader transfer and variance
we only track token cost without optimizing it

limitations.text: 固定对抗提示的排除不构成部署安全保证；作者指出，自适应攻击可能避开截断轨迹窗口或直接攻击未经验证的归因器。

evidence.quote: Our stress test shows that attribution can exclude fixed adversarial prompts, but this does not establish deployment safety. An adaptive adversary could act beyond the capped transcript window or exploit the unverified LLM attributer directly.

An LLM compares their transcripts and assigns each agent signed credit. CATS then updates link probabilities, prunes weak links and unreachable agents, and selects one fixed team for deployment.

Our selected topology G^{\star} improves mean accuracy over the strongest baseline, score-only heuristic search, by 5.3 points while using 54% fewer deployment tokens with matched candidate evaluations (Table 1 ).

Task scores, however, evaluate the team as a whole: a correct solution may contain unnecessary work, and a failed one may include useful contributions. Scores alone thus say little about which agents to keep.
We search for an optimized multi-agent topology as a subgraph of a hand-crafted complete directed acyclic graph specialized to a chosen problem domain (Figure 1 ).
Each edge e carries a logit \theta_{e} with sampling probability \alpha_{e}=\sigma(\theta_{e}) , initialized to a common \alpha_{0} .
At each step, we sample K topologies by independently drawing e\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\alpha_{e}) , rejecting graphs with nodes unreachable from the source.
An LLM attributer assigns each participating agent i in candidate k on task q a credit c_{k,q,i}\in[-1,1] (harmful to helpful) by comparing candidate rollouts on the same task.
The attributer sees task scores, length-capped agent outputs, tool calls, and the final artifact state (e.g., the coding environment), and runs in parallel across tasks.

Credits are normalized into per-agent advantages A_{k,i}=|Q_{k,i}|^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q_{k,i}}(c_{k,q,i}-b_{q}) , where Q_{k,i} holds the tasks with a credit for i in k and b_{q} is the mean credit over participating agents and candidates for task q .

Each edge (u,v) fired in candidate k is updated by \theta_{uv}\leftarrow\theta_{uv}+\eta A_{k,v} . Unfired non-source edges into an active agent v receive a smaller secondary update \theta_{uv}\leftarrow\theta_{uv}+\eta\rho A_{k,v} .

After each step we prune weak edges whose probability has fallen below the fraction \delta of its initial value (the pruning fraction ), E\leftarrow\{e\in E:\alpha_{e}\geq\delta\alpha_{0}\} , and remove nodes that are no longer reachable from the source.

After T steps we return the best final candidate G^{\star}=\arg\max_{k}\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{q}s_{k,q} over the step- T candidates, which are sampled under the accumulated priors. Ties are broken in favor of fewer agents and then the earlier candidate.

Our contributions are: (i) contrastive per-agent credit to guide team construction (Figure 1 ), (ii) higher mean accuracy and lower deployment token use than score-only search on two coding benchmarks with matched candidate evaluations (Table 1 )
(iii) a HotpotQA stress test where CATS excludes all poisoned agents in every run, while random search retains some at comparable accuracy (Table 2 ).
We adapt contrastive attribution [ 14 ] for BigCodeBench by grading the persisted code artifact instead of agent text. We also expose ordered, compact tool effects.

We compare against (i) a direct LLM call without tools, (ii) a ReAct [ 13 ] single agent, both with literature-derived system prompts (Appendix Table 6 ), (iii) a hand-crafted multi-agent system (MAS) designed before observing supergraph results (Appendix Figure 4(d) )

(iv) random topology search, and (v) a score-only heuristic search using CATS’s fired/unfired update and hyperparameters, with scalar task scores replacing agent credits. Both search baselines match K\times T candidate evaluations on the same tasks, not compute
Random search Draw 16 candidates at fixed \alpha=0.15 .

Assign A_{k} to every active agent and update edge logits using the same learning rate, unfired-edge rule, and pruning schedule as our method, but without LLM attribution. This heuristic omits the Bernoulli score-function factor I_{e}-\alpha_{e} required by REINFORCE [ 11 ] .
As an ablation, we also evaluate the pruned supergraph G_{\mathrm{p}} , consisting of all nodes and edges that remain after pruning.
Deploying G^{\star} instead of G_{\mathrm{p}} roughly halves coding deployment tokens, with higher mean accuracy on BigCodeBench and the same on MBPP (Table 1 ).
